subject: Dedicated capacity MAP: capacity planning & throughput targets
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmehealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Dedicated capacity MAP – capacity planning and throughput targets

Hi Alex + Priya —

Thanks for taking the time on the discovery calls this week. Per our conversation, I wanted to kick off a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to align stakeholders and milestones for a Dedicated capacity deployment. Goal is to get you to a pilot reservation (GPU pool + throughput SLOs) within 6–8 weeks, with a production go-live target contingent on the pilot outcomes.

High-level objectives for the MAP:
- Confirm throughput targets (p95 latency, tokens/sec) for your primary inference workloads
- Define GPU pool sizing and burst strategy for peak windows
- Agree roles/owners for procurement, security sign-off, and SRE acceptance tests
- Establish evaluation plan and success criteria for pilot -> production

Proposed roles (please edit):
- Customer PM: Alex Turner (primary owner for requirements)
- Customer SRE: Priya Shah (performance acceptance)
- Redwood AM/Lead SE: Rishi Malhotra (overall MAP owner)
- Redwood Solutions Engineer: Marissa Cole (throughput modeling + test harness)
- Redwood Runtime Lead: Markus Klein (quantization/kernel recommendations)

Initial asks:
1) Confirm whether the 1k concurrent LLM sessions estimate from our discovery is accurate (send any telemetry).
2) Share recent 95th-percentile latency targets and any SLA constraints (e.g., <200ms p95 for short prompts).
3) Availability for a 60-min capacity planning session the week of Mar 23 — we propose Tue/Wed morning PT.

Attached: rdw-dedicated-capacity-map-v1.pdf (MAP template) and baseline-throughput.xlsx (sample metrics) — these have a short intake questionnaire (first two tabs) to speed modeling.

Next step: If this looks right, Alex/Priya — can you confirm roles and pick 2 windows that work for a capacity planning call? We’ll come prepared with a proposed GPU pool and initial cost estimate.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated capacity MAP – capacity planning and throughput targets

Thanks Rishi — this is great and the proposed roles look right on our side. Quick clarifications from our SRE and product team: 

- The 1k concurrent sessions is a peak estimate for triage workflows; sustained concurrency is closer to 300–400.
- Our p95 latency target for short prompts (<128 tokens) is 250ms; for longer analysis prompts (~512 tokens) we target p95 < 700ms.
- We will need HIPAA-compliant logging and key management; Priya will lead the compliance checklist.

We can do Tue, Mar 24 09:30 PT or Wed, Mar 25 10:00 PT — Tue at 09:30 is preferred.

We’ll pull some telemetry and a small sample corpus for Marissa to run with.

Best,
Alex Turner
Product Lead, Clinical Insights | Acme Health
alex.turner@acmehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-8821

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated capacity MAP – capacity planning and throughput targets

Alex / Priya — thanks, and thanks for the telemetry you said you’d pull. I’m attaching a quick modeling workbook (baseline-throughput.xlsx) but pasted key assumptions here so we can iterate quickly on Tue: 

Baseline assumptions (editable):
- Primary model: med-size decoder LM, 32k context not used in pilot
- Avg prompt length: 80 tokens; avg response: 120 tokens
- Concurrent sessions (sustained): 350; peak conc. bursts: 1,000 for short windows
- Target p95 (short): 250ms; p95 (long): 700ms

Initial GPU pool proposal (pilot):
- 8x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs in a single pool with burst policy to add 4 GPUs for 30min windows and auto-scale by 1 GPU per additional 100 active sessions
- Continuous batching window: 20ms; KV-cache enabled across sessions belonging to the same user id prefix

Evaluation plan (pilot -> acceptance):
- Week 0: provisioning + sanity tests (throughput sanity harness)
- Week 1: load test with 50% of expected traffic (validate latency/ops)
- Week 2: end-to-end acceptance with production telemetry replay (SRE sign-off required)
- Success criteria: p95 latency within 10% of target for 3 consecutive days; no more than 1% error rate in responses

I’ve added a short checklist in the MAP PDF for HIPAA requirements (KMS/HSM, audit logs, retention). Markus — we’ll need quant recommendations for the pilot model; given latency constraints I’d suggest int8 with runtime kernel tuning first, and fallback to fp16 if quality regresses. Dev — can you confirm whether our VPC peering template meets Acme’s network baseline?

Attachment: baseline-throughput.xlsx (csv-style workbook)
Attachment: rdw-dedicated-capacity-map-v1.pdf (MAP + checklist)

Link to working MAP doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRDW-Acme-MAP
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company.com/deals/RDW-ACME-2026-07

See you Tue 24 Mar 09:30 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite once Alex confirms.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
